newsitem.title: UK: Russia's Lebed threatens West over NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed threatens West over NATO expansion.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed said Moscow would hit back at German and U.S. industrial interests in Russia if the West allowed NATO expansion to the former superpower's borders.

Lebed told London's Daily Telegraph newspaper in an interview published on Tuesday that Moscow felt deeply threatened by the Alliance's plans to allow former Communist Bloc states to become members and suggested Germany was trying to build a new empire in the East.
"We follow the strategy closely and will react accordingly. I am telling you that I will therefore have to reconsider the proper attitude to the United States and Germany," he said.
"Let there be no mistake. German and American industrial interests in Russia will suffer directly as a result of enlargement plans."
Officials from Moscow and NATO met last week in Vienna to hammer out a compromise over the Alliance's plans to accept former Warsaw Pact states as members but the two sides remain far apart.

Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov last week made clear that the stationing of NATO troops and weapons closer to Russia's borders was unacceptable. Hungary, Poland and the Czech republic are front-runners to join NATO, probably next year.
Lebed said he would explain his opposition to expansion plans when he visited NATO headquarters early next month.

"With the enlargement of NATO and of the European Union, the whole of central and eastern Europe will come under German economic and political domination," said the outspoken ex-general, who came third in this year's presidential polls.
"Is this the work of the new generation of post-unification policymakers, building a Fourth Reich?" he asked.
"We cannot forget history. The whole relationship between Germany and Russia, which has been successful in the past, will have to be reviewed if NATO enlargement proceeds."
President Boris Yeltsin appointed Lebed as his security adviser three months ago and the gruff former paratroop general has made no secret of his own presidential ambitions.
